title: Feeling Like a Fraud? Good. Fake It Anyway.
title_alternatives: You're Not Ready. Do It Anyway. (Fake It Till You Make It)
Why Your Plan B Is Why You're Stuck (Burn the Boats)
Imposter Syndrome Is Lying to You. Here's the Cheat Code.
description:
You don't need to feel ready. Nobody does. The people you envy were all faking it once.

5 minutes on why "fake it till you make it" is a real strategy (not a cringe quote), and the one move that makes it work: burn your boats.

You'll learn:
- why waiting to feel confident is the actual trap
- Ben Franklin's weekly "virtue report card" (yes, really)
- Type 1 vs Type 2 crazy: which big dreams are worth chasing
- why your Plan B is quietly killing your Plan A
- the rule that turns every failure into data

Your turn: what's YOUR Type 1 crazy belief? The one that sounds unhinged but normal humans have done it before. Drop it below and tell us the first ugly step you'll take this week.

CHAPTERS
0:00 you're not ready (nobody is)
0:40 Ben Franklin's notebook of shame
1:53 Type 1 vs Type 2 crazy (the dragon test)
2:45 Burn the boats (your Plan B is a trap)
3:50 Action produces information
4:28 The belief meter

SOURCES
- Benjamin Franklin, The Autobiography: the thirteen virtues and his weekly chart
- Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian: Xiang Yu at the Battle of Julu, 207 BC (sank the boats, broke the cooking pots, three days of food)
- Hernan Cortes, 1519: the scuttling of his ships (often retold as "burning" them)
- Thomas Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict (1960): commitment devices
- Ideas credited in the video: Varun Mayya ("Type 1 / Type 2 crazy") and Brian Armstrong ("Action produces information")

Animated in a hand-drawn stick-figure style. Narration is an AI voice.
